ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR diluted share counts are in ordinary shares while the Nasdaq price ($51.33) is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x2 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price. Using the pre-September-2024 5:1 ratio would overstate per-ADS owner's earnings 2.5x.
ads_ratio.source: Ryanair Holdings plc Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025 (SEC filing, accession 0001558370-25-007966), Item 12 (Description of Securities Other than Equity Securities): during FY25 the Board approved a change to the ADS ratio so that one ADS is now equal to two Ordinary Shares, a 2:1 ratio (previously 5:1); the ratio change was effected in September 2024

moat_against: Commodity seat bought on price alone — zero switching costs, no loyalty lock-in
Fuel exposure: 20% unhedged FY27 volume spiked above $150/bbl in Q1 FY27
Rising EU environmental taxes (~€300m additional expected in FY27)
Boeing delivery delays have repeatedly capped traffic growth
Regulatory risk: Italian AGCM €256m fine (appealed; €85m provided in FY26)
ATC strikes, geopolitics and fare cyclicality hit earnings directly
moat_for: Structural unit-cost advantage vs EU rivals (single-type fleet, high-density B737-8200 Gamechangers)
Scale: Europe's largest airline by passengers (208.4m in FY26)
Ancillary revenue engine (~€24 per passenger in FY26)
Debt-free / net-cash balance sheet after May 2026 bond repayment
Disciplined fuel hedging (80% of FY27 needs at ~$67/bbl)
Profitable through cycles that bankrupted less efficient rivals
moat_justification: Europe's structural low-cost carrier: a genuine, cycle-tested unit-cost advantage (single-type 737 fleet, high-density Gamechanger aircraft, direct distribution, ancillary revenue engine, disciplined fuel hedging) that has kept it profitable through shocks that bankrupted rivals, plus the scale of Europe's largest passenger airline and a debt-free, net-cash balance sheet after the May 2026 bond repayment. Capped at 6 because the product is a commodity seat bought purely on price — there are no switching costs, no loyalty lock-in and no network-effect moat; fares fell 6% in Q1 FY27 despite the cost lead, and the economics remain hostage to fuel prices, EU environmental taxes, ATC disruption, Boeing deliveries and geopolitics.
name: Ryanair Holdings plc
one_liner: Europe's lowest-cost airline, moat 6/10, debt-free — quality is not the issue; at $51.33 the weighted IRR is 12.49% (Tier C), below the 15% hurdle; it clears 15% at the weighted IV@15% of $40.23.
